title: SCHEDULING: is the frontier unresolvable because the scheduler picks the wrong matches? (zero calls)

plain_description.what: No calls. For the six pairs among the top 4 models on about 3,400 questions, the test compared how often the answer key can settle a match when the two models' own final answers differ versus when they agree.
plain_description.why: It asks whether the frontier models cannot be told apart because the scheduler wastes matches on questions with no signal.
plain_description.information: If informative matches sit almost only where answers differ, judging only those cuts cost with no loss. Result: done, descriptive. Answers differ on 16.9% of question pairs. Filtering on that keeps 99.8% of all decidable pairs while judging only 16.9% of matches, with no answer key needed. This works for multiple-choice and checkable tasks, not open-ended generation.
